items.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: In New York, Phil performed and recorded with a long list of jazz veterans including Bob Wilber, Benny Goodman, Mel Torme and Maxine Sullivan.

ctx.x: Phil Flanigan is one of the most in-demand bassists in jazz today. A native of Geneva, New York, he found fertile playing ground in Providence with tenor saxophonist Scott Hamilton. With guitarist Chris Flory and drummer Chuck Riggs, a working quartet evolved that eventually recorded over twenty albums and helped renew interest in mainstream jazz. In New York, Phil performed and recorded with a long list of jazz veterans including Bob Wilber, Benny Goodman, Mel Torme and Maxine Sullivan. His passion is preserving…
Phil was interviewed in San Diego, California on February 15, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
